# sgmean

`sgmean` computes the trimmed mean using a proportional discount method
on the extremes, replicating the behavior of Statgraphics software.

Unlike R's built-in `mean(..., trim)`, which removes boundary values
entirely, `sgmean` applies a weighted reduction — producing results
consistent with Statgraphics.

`sgmean` is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by
Statgraphics.

## Installation

The version on CRAN is 0.1.2 (the function `sgmean()` only). The development
version on GitHub is 0.2.0 and adds inference, diagnostics and descriptive
statistics (see below); it will reach CRAN later.

```r
# CRAN version (0.1.2)
install.packages("sgmean")

# Development version (0.2.0)
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jcarlosgaviria/sgmean")
```

## Usage

```r
library(sgmean)

x <- c(2, 4, 6, 8, 100)

# sgmean method (Statgraphics compatible)
sgmean(x, trim = 0.05)

# Base R method (different result)
mean(x, trim = 0.05)
```

## New in 0.2.0 (GitHub version)

```r
x <- c(850, 920, 980, 1050, 1120, 1180, 1250, 1320, 1400, 1480, 1550,
       1700, 1850, 2100, 8500)

# Proportional trimmed mean vs. base R
sgmean(x, trim = 0.10)          # 1365.833
mean(x, trim = 0.10)            # 1376.923 (R truncates k = 1.5 to 1)
diagnose_truncation(x, trim = 0.10)
plot_trim_profile(x)

# Inference for the trimmed mean (Yuen-type tests return 'htest' objects)
y <- c(900, 1010, 1100, 1190, 1250, 1330, 1420, 1500, 1610, 1720, 1830,
       1950, 2100, 2300, 2600)   # a second sample
ttest_trimmed(x, mu0 = 1300, trim = 0.10)
ci_trimmed(x, trim = 0.10)
se_trimmed(x, trim = 0.10)
ttest_rel_trimmed(x, y, trim = 0.10)     # paired samples
ttest_ind_trimmed(x, y, trim = 0.10)     # two samples; also gives effect_size
effect_size_trimmed(x, y, trim = 0.10)   # robust standardized difference

# Statgraphics-style descriptive statistics (29 results; English or Spanish labels)
sg_summary(x, trim = 0.10)
print(sg_summary(x, trim = 0.10), lang = "es")
set_language("es")
```

Also available: `winsorized_mean()`, `winsorized_sigma()`, `sg_quantile()`
(Hyndman-Fan types 1-9, default type 2), `quartiles()`, `iqr()`,
`geometric_mean()`, `dam()`, `sbi()`, `skewness()`, `kurtosis()`, `cv()`,
`std_error()` and `sg_mode()`. Three functions carry the prefix `sg_`
(`sg_quantile`, `sg_mode`, `sg_summary`) so that they do not mask
`stats::quantile`, `base::mode` and `summary`.

The standard error and the test for fractional `k = trim * n` interpolate
between the classical estimators for `floor(k)` and `floor(k) + 1` values per
tail. They coincide with the classical Tukey-McLaughlin / Yuen results when
`k` is an integer; for fractional `k` they are a heuristic supported by
simulation, not a proven result. See `NEWS.md` for details.

## Python

The same methods are available in Python:
[sgmean on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/sgmean/) and
[sgmean-python on GitHub](https://github.com/jcarlosgaviria/sgmean-python).
The two packages share reference values in their test suites.
